rationale: The child is a short statutory reporting letter approving an emergency undertaking by the Virgin Islands Corporation and explaining the specific mismanagement, lease termination, operational necessity, and expected revenues. No candidate shares its reporting formula, narrative structure, emergency-approval mechanism, or Virgin Islands Corporation machinery. C20 is closest because it concerns Navy and Interior control of federal property in the Virgin Islands, but it supplies only related historical subject matter rather than a concrete drafting template. C11 and C02 likewise concern transfers or administration of federal property, but their operative legal machinery and language are materially different.

shared_material.child_excerpt: These properties had been transferred by the Navy to the Department of the Interior for operation and management under a revocable permit.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: certain other lands, buildings, improvements, and furnishings in the Virgin Islands temporarily [were transferred] to the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Interior
shared_material.explanation: C20 shares the setting of Navy-to-Interior control over federal property in the Virgin Islands, but the wording, legal mechanism, and document function differ; this is contextual overlap rather than evidence of reused drafting.

shared_material.child_excerpt: transferred by the Navy to the Department of the Interior
shared_material.parent_excerpt: shall hereafter be vested in and exercised by the Secretary of the Interior
shared_material.explanation: C11 also uses Navy-to-Interior transfer machinery, but it concerns control of Treasury funds under submerged-lands statutes, not property management or an emergency undertaking report.

shared_material.child_excerpt: management of the Federal properties in the Virgin Islands
shared_material.parent_excerpt: property, real and personal, owned by the United States in Guam
shared_material.explanation: C02 concerns federal property administration in an insular territory, but it is a detailed reservation and jurisdiction order with no distinctive language or operative sequence matching the child.
